decisions.focus: Prototype demos, with reuse before new implementation
reuseNow: Existing Sealos OpenDesign service and scenarios
decisions.unattended: One Twitch event triggers one OBS alert while chat is closed
decisions.completion: Demonstrate the issue's visible result, record limits, then merge its implementation. Existing upstream work alone does not prove the Stream Machine hookup.

milestones.title: V1 Working demos
milestones.description: Four core demos, with OpenDesign and its HyperFrames workflow reused in parallel. No general framework prerequisite.

milestones.title: V2 Clips games and artwork
milestones.description: Download a clip, add media/game details, and use optional artwork tools.

milestones.title: V3 More streamer workflows
milestones.description: Add useful analytics and native UI conveniences without making prototype work wait for public distribution.

milestones.title: Later Polish and sharing
milestones.description: Shared abstractions, multi-user hosting, broader recovery, and public distribution when a working demo needs them.

tracks.name: Shared code later
tracks.goal: Extract shared helpers only after working demos need the same code.

tracks.name: Twitch title
tracks.goal: Reuse Twitch OAuth and change one channel title after preview.

tracks.name: OBS alert
tracks.goal: Connect to the running OBS instance and show one test alert.

tracks.name: Stream Deck button
tracks.goal: Add and press one button in a dedicated test profile.

tracks.name: Event to OBS
tracks.goal: Show an OBS alert from one Twitch event while chat is closed.

tracks.name: Clips and games
tracks.goal: Turn clips and game data into useful streamer assets.

tracks.name: OpenDesign and HyperFrames
tracks.goal: Reuse the existing Sealos OpenDesign service and its HyperFrames workflow.

tracks.name: Use Stream Machine
tracks.goal: Open the plugin and reach a working demo without unnecessary setup.

tracks.name: Sharing later
tracks.goal: Show the demo first. Add sharing and production work when needed.

items.title: Extract shared code only when two demos need it
items.scope: Keep duplicate code small once the first demos work.
accept: Find a helper that two working demos actually use.
Extract that helper without changing either demo's result.
Keep the relevant tests passing and name both callers in the PR.
items.outcome: Keep duplicate code small once the first demos work.
items.reuse: The existing mock core and the code written for the first real demos.
items.limit: Do not create a complete account, event, asset, or recipe framework in advance. This issue blocks no demo.

items.title: Shelved: automatic provider selection
items.scope: This separate framework task is no longer part of the prototype.
items.outcome: This separate framework task is no longer part of the prototype.
items.reuse: Keep the existing demo code.
items.limit: #25, #28, #31, and #43 choose their own existing connection. Reopen only when repeated working demos justify shared machinery.

items.title: Shelved: generic recipe planner
items.scope: This separate framework task is no longer part of the prototype.
items.outcome: This separate framework task is no longer part of the prototype.
items.reuse: Keep the existing demo code.
items.limit: #27, #30, and #32 provide the previews their demos need. Reopen only when repeated working demos justify shared machinery.

items.title: Shelved: general-purpose recipe runner
items.scope: This separate framework task is no longer part of the prototype.
items.outcome: This separate framework task is no longer part of the prototype.
items.reuse: Keep the existing demo code.
items.limit: #33 and #36–#38 implement only the execution needed by those demos. Reopen only when repeated working demos justify shared machinery.

items.title: Use the existing Twitch login in Stream Machine
items.scope: Stream Machine shows the Twitch account that the existing OAuth flow connects.
accept: Record how Stream Machine maps the current user to the existing connection without copying tokens into tools or UI.
Show the connected account and granted permissions through Stream Machine.
Keep the existing OAuth checks passing and verify the new hookup with the creator account.
items.outcome: Stream Machine shows the Twitch account that the existing OAuth flow connects.
items.reuse: Reuse TwitchService, ConnectionStore, and the verified TwitchCon OAuth flow. PR #48 already implemented login, encryption, validation, and refresh.
items.limit: Do not rebuild OAuth. Adapt only the identity or runtime boundary that Stream Machine needs. Scope upgrades use the existing flow.

items.title: Read my current Twitch title and category
items.scope: Ask Stream Machine for the connected channel's current title and category.
accept: Return the expected broadcaster, title, and category.
Show a clear connection or permission error instead of demo data when access is missing.
Verify one real read without changing the channel.
items.outcome: Ask Stream Machine for the connected channel's current title and category.
items.reuse: Use the existing Twitch connection and client. The supplied Twitch MCP repo can provide a read-operation reference.
items.limit: Do not wait for clips, videos, chat metadata, or a provider registry.

items.title: Change my Twitch title after preview
items.scope: Preview one new title, apply it, and see the title read back from Twitch.
accept: Preview the exact account, current title, and proposed title without writing.
If channel:manage:broadcast is missing, request it through the existing OAuth flow.
Apply one authorized update to that account and read back the expected title.
items.outcome: Preview one new title, apply it, and see the title read back from Twitch.
items.reuse: Use the existing OAuth implementation and the current-channel read in #26.
items.limit: Do not expose credentials or accept another account as the target. No generic recipe engine is required.

items.title: Connect Stream Machine to the running OBS instance
items.scope: List the scenes and sources from the user's running OBS instance.
accept: Return the expected scene and source names from the running instance.
Explain whether the MCP server or OBS is unavailable when a connection fails.
Record the selected provider and connection settings without exposing secrets.
items.outcome: List the scenes and sources from the user's running OBS instance.
items.reuse: Reuse the existing TwitchCon OBS setup and checks. Use one suitable local MCP provider from agentic-obs or obs-twitch-mcp.
items.limit: Do not start another OBS instance, change authentication, start Twitch chat automation, or change a broadcast.

items.title: Shelved: add another OBS server only for a missing feature
items.scope: Revisit the alternative OBS server only if the selected provider cannot perform a required demo action.
items.outcome: Revisit the alternative OBS server only if the selected provider cannot perform a required demo action.
items.reuse: Compare the supplied OBS repositories before adding a dependency.
items.limit: The current demo does not require a second server. If reopened, first remove unwanted chat/moderation startup and token output from any adopted path.

items.title: Show one alert in OBS
items.scope: Show an existing alert in a dedicated OBS test source and change its message or replay it.
accept: Select a dedicated test source and preview the intended change.
Show the alert with the expected text or replay behavior.
Remove or restore only the test resource and confirm the broadcast and existing scene settings are unchanged.
items.outcome: Show an existing alert in a dedicated OBS test source and change its message or replay it.
items.reuse: Reuse the accepted TwitchCon alert artifacts and the existing OBS setup. Do not require a new design or render service.
items.limit: If the running OBS variant needs a different visible-test procedure, record it before touching the program scene.

items.title: Read my Stream Deck profiles and actions
items.scope: See the connected deck, its profiles, and actions that can be reused.
accept: Identify the intended device and its button or dial layout.
List profiles and at least one existing configured action.
Report missing device or server clearly without changing profiles.
items.outcome: See the connected deck, its profiles, and actions that can be reused.
items.reuse: Use the supplied streamdeck-mcp profile tools and the user's existing hardware.
items.limit: Do not restart the app, claim the USB device, generate scripts, or write a profile during this read.

items.title: Preview one Stream Deck test button
items.scope: See where one button will go and what it will do.
accept: Show the target test profile, button position, and chosen action.
Reject a position that does not fit the device.
Produce the preview without changing a profile or creating a script.
items.outcome: See where one button will go and what it will do.
items.reuse: Reuse a configured action from #31 and a copy of a test profile.
items.limit: Keep the first action independent of Twitch. No reusable page-planning framework is required.

items.title: Add one working Stream Deck button
items.scope: Press one new button in a dedicated test profile and see its expected action.
accept: Back up a dedicated test profile and explain any required app restart.
Write one previewed button, switch to the test profile, and verify the button's action on the device.
Restore the test profile and confirm unrelated profiles remain unchanged.
items.outcome: Press one new button in a dedicated test profile and see its expected action.
items.reuse: Use the existing profile writer and a configured action rather than a new device integration.
items.limit: Never overwrite the active profile or run an arbitrary generated script.

items.title: Subscribe to one Twitch event
items.scope: Subscribe the connected Twitch account to one event used by the alert demo.
accept: Choose an event that can be tested with the creator account and request its required permission through the existing flow.
Create the subscription and report its actual enabled state.
Stop or remove the test subscription cleanly.
items.outcome: Subscribe the connected Twitch account to one event used by the alert demo.
items.reuse: Reuse the existing OAuth tokens and validation. Add only the EventSub connection and subscription this demo needs.
items.limit: Keep the first transport local WebSocket. Broad event catalogs and hosted webhook delivery can wait.

items.title: Log Twitch events and ignore duplicate messages
items.scope: Turn a received event into a small record that the alert code can consume.
accept: Record the event ID, type, account, time, and alert data.
Feed the same test message twice and produce only one alert request.
Show disconnects or missing data instead of silently reporting success.
items.outcome: Turn a received event into a small record that the alert code can consume.
items.reuse: Use example EventSub messages first. Connect the handler to #34 for the real demonstration.
items.limit: Do not build a general queue platform. A small local record and duplicate check are enough for the demo.

items.title: Keep the alert worker running after chat closes
items.scope: Start a local process that can still receive an event and call OBS after the chat closes.
accept: Start and stop the worker with an explicit command and show whether it is running.
Close chat and prove that a test event still reaches the worker.
Give the worker its own vetted MCP or OBS connection and keep tokens out of output.
items.outcome: Start a local process that can still receive an event and call OBS after the chat closes.
items.reuse: Reuse the current OAuth validation and an existing OBS connection path.
items.limit: The desktop must stay awake and the worker must stay running. Automatic OS startup, distributed queues, and a cloud bridge are not required.

items.title: Arm and pause the one event-to-alert rule
items.scope: Explicitly enable one event-to-alert rule, then stop it when needed.
accept: Show the selected Twitch account, event, and OBS test source before activation.
Require explicit activation and provide a visible pause or stop control.
After pause or revoked access, prove that later test events cannot trigger the action.
items.outcome: Explicitly enable one event-to-alert rule, then stop it when needed.
items.reuse: Keep the rule beside the local worker rather than building a general permissions engine.
items.limit: Restrict the demo to the selected account and test source. Broad unattended permissions, arbitrary commands, and broadcast controls are excluded.

items.title: Show an OBS alert from Twitch while chat is closed
items.scope: Receive a real Twitch event and see its OBS alert with chat closed.
accept: Activate the one test rule, close chat, and produce a real subscribed Twitch event.
See the expected alert and a matching worker log entry.
Repeat a duplicate test message and then pause the rule to verify that neither case produces an extra alert.
items.outcome: Receive a real Twitch event and see its OBS alert with chat closed.
items.reuse: Combine the existing account connection, the local worker, and the tested OBS alert action.
items.limit: Use only the selected test resource. Do not change broadcasting or unrelated scenes.

items.title: Download one Twitch clip
items.scope: Choose one authorized clip and get a usable video file.
accept: Request the required clip permission through the existing OAuth flow if needed.
Download one authorized clip and play the resulting file.
Return the clip source and file location, with a clear error for expired links or unavailable formats.
items.outcome: Choose one authorized clip and get a usable video file.
items.reuse: Use the existing Twitch login and the official clip download API.
items.limit: Start with one clip. Batch downloads and a general asset store can wait.

items.title: Show details or a transcript for one clip
items.scope: Read useful metadata or an available transcript from one public media URL.
accept: Return the media title, source, and requested metadata or transcript.
Report when a transcript or provider is unavailable.
Keep the service private and verify one URL without making other workflows depend on it.
items.outcome: Read useful metadata or an available transcript from one public media URL.
items.reuse: Use yt-media-info-mcp as an optional provider.
items.limit: This provider does not download media.

items.title: Find a game and its artwork
items.scope: Find one game's details and artwork for a stream recipe.
accept: Show the game's name, relevant details, artwork reference, and source.
Map Twitch categories through igdb_id instead of treating Twitch and IGDB IDs as the same.
Record which provider receives the request and verify one real lookup.
items.outcome: Find one game's details and artwork for a stream recipe.
items.reuse: Review the supplied mcp-igdb relay before choosing it or a small direct IGDB call.
items.limit: Do not build a general game catalog. Streamer OAuth is not required for this lookup.

items.title: Show one useful streaming metric with its source
items.scope: Display one named metric that the available APIs or collected events can actually support.
accept: Choose one metric and state its source, time range, timezone, and known gaps.
Show the calculation for a small sample and verify its result.
Label estimates and unavailable data clearly.
items.outcome: Display one named metric that the available APIs or collected events can actually support.
items.reuse: Reuse Twitch reads, worker event records, or a user-provided report.
items.limit: Do not promise the full Creator Dashboard analytics API or build a broad analytics warehouse.

items.title: Make an asset with the existing OpenDesign service
items.scope: Choose an existing OpenDesign scenario from Stream Machine and receive its output.
accept: Restore or verify the existing tool connection and list an installed scenario or accepted project.
Pass one small brief through Stream Machine into the existing service using an isolated test project.
Return the resulting artifact and report success or failure from that run.
items.outcome: Choose an existing OpenDesign scenario from Stream Machine and receive its output.
items.reuse: Reuse the running Sealos service and installed stream-alert-authoring and stream-overlay-authoring scenarios.
items.limit: No new container, daemon, authentication system, or copied administrative credentials. Prior accepted runs are reuse evidence, not proof of this new hookup.

items.title: Render a short video with OpenDesign HyperFrames
items.scope: Use OpenDesign's existing HyperFrames workflow to produce and play one short video.
accept: Submit a small system-font composition through the existing HyperFrames workflow.
Follow the returned task until completion or failure without launching duplicate jobs.
Play the returned MP4 and check its duration and dimensions. Keep the editable composition accessible.
items.outcome: Use OpenDesign's existing HyperFrames workflow to produce and play one short video.
items.reuse: Reuse the integrated composition, render, wait, and artifact path in the current OpenDesign deployment.
items.limit: Do not install a separate vanilla HyperFrames renderer by default. Existing HTML alert tests do not prove this video-render path.

items.title: Make one artwork draft with the Canva plugin
items.scope: Create one thumbnail or schedule draft using the existing Canva connection.
accept: Discover the actual connection and a supported design operation.
Create one isolated test design from a small brief.
Return the design or export link and show a useful error when Canva is unavailable.
items.outcome: Create one thumbnail or schedule draft using the existing Canva connection.
items.reuse: Use the provider's supported plugin tools and keep its credentials with the provider.
items.limit: No automatic publishing, provider bundling, or dependency on Twitch.

items.title: Open and use Stream Machine in the native app
items.scope: Open the installed plugin and use its tools and view in the intended host.
accept: Record which installed version opens and which tools are available.
Open the native view and complete one harmless demo action.
Record any unsupported host feature without treating browser preview as native verification.
items.outcome: Open the installed plugin and use its tools and view in the intended host.
items.reuse: Use the existing package and installation rather than creating a duplicate plugin.
items.limit: Check the host used for this demo first. A complete mobile and web compatibility matrix can wait.

items.title: Help me choose and start a working demo
items.scope: Onboarding points to the working Twitch, OBS, Stream Deck, or creative path with the fewest setup steps.
accept: Show what is already available and what the selected demo still needs.
Allow unrelated setup to be skipped, so OBS or Stream Deck does not wait for Twitch.
Get the user to one harmless working check and keep unattended activation separate.
items.outcome: Onboarding points to the working Twitch, OBS, Stream Deck, or creative path with the fewest setup steps.
items.reuse: Discover existing accounts, services, and plugins first.
items.limit: No mandatory installation of every provider or full cross-device onboarding system.

items.title: Add one native shortcut that improves a demo
items.scope: Choose a useful native convenience, such as a saved setting, recipe mention, or deep link.
accept: Choose the shortcut from actual demo friction rather than implementing every extension.
Verify it in a host that supports it.
Keep a usable chat or in-app fallback where it is unsupported.
items.outcome: Choose a useful native convenience, such as a saved setting, recipe mention, or deep link.
items.reuse: Use the existing MCP App and supported OpenAI Extensions.
items.limit: Do not make the first demos wait for settings, mentions, file handlers, and deep links as a bundle.

items.title: Show the four core demos end to end
items.scope: Run a short demonstration of Twitch title update, OBS alert, Stream Deck button, and chat-closed automation.
accept: Show the real title update and its read-back.
Show the OBS alert and press the working Stream Deck test button.
Close chat and show a real Twitch event trigger the OBS alert. Record the known limits and cleanup.
items.outcome: Run a short demonstration of Twitch title update, OBS alert, Stream Deck button, and chat-closed automation.
items.reuse: Use the existing services and the small implementations completed by those demo issues.
items.limit: OpenDesign and HyperFrames are parallel V1 reuse wins. They can finish independently of the four core demonstrations. Broad production hardening is not a release requirement.

items.title: Add shared hosting only if invited testers need it
items.scope: Provide the access method that an actual invited test requires.
accept: Use the access decision in #54 to choose local installs, shared hosting, or both.
If hosting is needed, verify that one tester cannot access another tester's account or credentials.
Record installation and disconnect behavior for that supported path.
items.outcome: Provide the access method that an actual invited test requires.
items.reuse: Prefer the existing deployments and login code before adding infrastructure.
items.limit: No new hosted platform or cloud-to-desktop bridge without a concrete test requirement.

items.title: Try the working demos with one invited streamer
items.scope: Have one invited streamer complete the selected demos on their setup.
accept: Install or connect through the chosen access path.
Complete one selected demo and record the steps that caused confusion.
Confirm account ownership and record defects as small follow-up issues.
items.outcome: Have one invited streamer complete the selected demos on their setup.
items.reuse: Reuse the working package and documented provider setup.
items.limit: Do not require every optional provider or advanced Extension. Hosted implementation is required only if #54 selects it.

items.title: Prepare a public release after the demos are useful
items.scope: Prepare the subset of working recipes selected for public distribution.
accept: Review the selected providers' permissions, licenses, and data handling.
Make listing claims match tested behavior and supported platforms.
Prepare installation examples and the submission package for the selected scope.
items.outcome: Prepare the subset of working recipes selected for public distribution.
items.reuse: Use the verified package, provider connections, and demo records.
items.limit: Public publication is a separate action. Do not wait for every optional integration before preparing a smaller useful release.

items.title: Add the next Twitch read needed by a demo
items.scope: Add one useful stream, clip, video, or chat-metadata read.
accept: Choose one read that a concrete recipe needs.
Return the real result with its source and clear unavailable or rate-limit errors.
Verify one harmless record and keep the title demo working.
items.outcome: Add one useful stream, clip, video, or chat-metadata read.
items.reuse: Reuse the existing connection and reviewed operations from twitch-mcp-server.
items.limit: No full Twitch wrapper or undocumented archived-comments GraphQL.

items.title: Choose how one invited streamer will connect
items.scope: Decide the smallest access setup for the first invited tester.
accept: Name the tester's required devices and demos.
Choose local installation, hosted access, or both, and explain the account boundary.
Record any extra work that the chosen test actually requires.
items.outcome: Decide the smallest access setup for the first invited tester.
items.reuse: Start with independent local installs and existing hosted services.
items.limit: No speculative multi-tenant platform or mandatory hosted service.
